population.note: FICTIONAL. Base is about 276M adults. Current users are 37.1%, about 102.4M. Ever-users are 48.5%, about 133.9M. That leaves 11.4 points, about 31.5M, who used and are now off, and about 142M who have never used. Cycling arithmetic: about 19.0 points of current users are on a second or later course, and about 5.0 points of the off-now group restarted at least once and stopped again, so (19.0 + 5.0)/48.5 ≈ 49.5% have cycled. That fits ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart within a year. Ever-use rose 8.5 points against a limit of 11.6, and current use rose 8.6. Age check: 18–29: 21% × 52M = 10.9M; 30–49: 42% × 92M = 38.6M; 50–64: 54.1% × 61M = 33.0M; 65+: 28% × 71M = 19.9M. Total ≈ 102.4M = 37.1%. The jump in the 65+ band from 21% to 28% has two causes: the 2036 tirzepatide MCI indication (≈1.6M users coded for MCI by year end) and the 50 mg pill, partly offset by bone pauses and post-NAION stops. Income thirds average (41 + 37.5 + 32.8)/3 ≈ 37.1. The middle third grew least relative to need, because employer retreat hit it hardest. Its growth came from the $199 portal maintenance price and from diabetes-code coverage. Bottom-third growth came from Medicaid (14.0M) and imports (9.0M); import growth slowed as the portal price fell. The off-now 31.5M are mostly people who lost employer weight coverage in 2035–36 and did not move to cash, plus bone pauses, NAION stops, GI quitters and conviction-quitters from the backlash. The never-users skew under-30, rural, contraindicated, and increasingly toward deliberate refusers. Pediatric use is 1.6% of ≈73M ≈ 1.17M: ≈1.06M adolescents 12+ and ≈110k children aged 6–11 after the Dec 2035 semaglutide approval, more than half of them on Medicaid under EPSDT. About half of US children now live with at least one parent who is on the drug or cycling off it.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. The statutory terms of the Part D obesity benefit are unchanged: $199/month, $50 copay, counselling visit, eligibility at BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity. Medicare pays 19.3% of fills, ≈19.8M users (≈18.2M aged 65+ and ≈1.6M disabled under-65): ≈7.6M for diabetes and ≈12.2M under the obesity benefit, including ≈1.6M with an MCI code under the new tirzepatide label, which uses the same eligibility rules. Obesity-benefit spend: 12.2M × $199 × 12 ≈ $29.1B gross. Copays are 12.2M × $50 × 12 ≈ $7.3B, so the program pays ≈$21.8B. All Medicare incretin fills: 19.8M × $199 × 12 ≈ $47.3B gross. CMS has not decided whether the tirzepatide/bimagrumab combination falls under the $199 statutory rate. Lilly argues that bimagrumab is a separate non-incretin biologic. For now Medicare beneficiaries can get the combination only by paying cash. Medicaid: the same 31 states plus DC remain on the 90% match and the continuation standard. Medicaid pays 13.7% of fills, ≈14.0M users × $199 × 12 ≈ $33.4B gross before supplemental rebates. EPSDT obliges coverage of medically necessary under-12 semaglutide in every state.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $5–30/month, including generic oral semaglutide at 50 mg strength from 2035. Tirzepatide copies have appeared in China and Bangladesh. China: Chinese API still underlies most of the gray trade, along with 'research-grade' retatrutide and now bimagrumab-labelled vials of unknown content. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 40–70. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt have generics. US: still no generic. FDA declared the first filer's 180-day exclusivity forfeited in Aug 2035, but the D.C. Circuit stayed the decision pending appeal. Rival filers' settlement dates are contingent on that exclusivity running out or being forfeited, so they cannot launch. The appeal was argued in Apr 2036 and has not been decided.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline. Under the Jul 2035 three-year portal commitments with HHS, direct-portal maintenance prices fell. Injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide now cost $199–249, down from $249–329. The Wegovy 50 mg pill is $199, down from $299, and the oral starters stay at $149–150. Retatrutide is $349 direct ($1,299 list, down from $1,649), amycretin $399, MariTide $449/month-equivalent, and tirzepatide/bimagrumab $549 direct ($1,499 list). PBM net fell to ≈$170–185. Payer mix of ≈102.4M users: commercial 26.9% (27.5M); Medicare 19.3% (19.8M); Medicaid 13.7% (14.0M); cash/direct 31.3% (32.1M, including ≈5.8M 'calm' and 'focus' subscribers); imported/counterfeit 8.8% (9.0M). Sum = 102.4M, 100%. Employer coverage for weight management fell from 64% to 46% of employers. Diabetes, cardiovascular, sleep-apnoea and CKD codes stay covered in nearly every plan, so ≈62% of commercial fills now run under non-obesity codes, up from ≈45%. Clinicians call this 'code migration'. About 85% of the employers still covering use gated designs, and about a third add tenure gates. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand. Routes: ≈44% of users are on daily orals.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, incl. 7.2 mg; pediatric 6–11 from Dec 2035)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro; MCI-to-dementia risk reduction label from Mar 2036)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist plus activin type II receptor antibody, co-packaged weekly pen and monthly subcutaneous injection (tirzepatide/bimagrumab, approved Dec 2035)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GIPR-antagonist/GLP-1 agonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill incl. 50 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: reduction of risk of progression from mild cognitive impairment to dementia in adults with obesity or type 2 diabetes (tirzepatide, Mar 2036)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm', 'focus' and 'craving freedom' subscriptions (low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo, ≈5.8M subscribers)
'brain-protection' tirzepatide or 50 mg pill in normal-weight older adults with memory complaints, cash-pay through concierge and telehealth
smoking and vaping cessation (SHAPS trial still enrolling)
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens in concierge practices
gray-market 'research' retatrutide and bimagrumab-labelled vials among gym and physique users
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, still anecdotal
planned 'drug holidays' and dose-down weekends, now routine enough that telehealth apps schedule them
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Muscle-preserving combination: bimagrumab combinations were in phase 3 with no filing at the start of this step. Lilly filed tirzepatide/bimagrumab in Dec 2034 on the phase 3 result: ≈22% mean loss, with lean mass ≈12% of loss on DEXA versus ≈33% on tirzepatide alone. FDA approved it in Dec 2035, 12 months after filing. Its label claims preserved lean mass, not improved strength or fracture risk. The 'skinny-frail problem solved' line comes from marketing and is not in the label. ≈1.1M users by end-2036. Pediatric: Novo filed the semaglutide ages 6–11 sNDA in Dec 2034 on STEP Young and received approval in Dec 2035, with baseline and annual DEXA and growth monitoring in the label. Cognition: Lilly's 3-year tirzepatide MCI trial (n≈3,800, adults 60+ with obesity or T2D) read out in Nov 2034. Conversion to dementia had a hazard ratio of 0.79, and the CDR-SB difference was 0.4 points at 36 months, modest but significant. Lilly filed the sNDA in Dec 2034, and it was approved in Mar 2036 after a review extension. Semaglutide's earlier Alzheimer's trials remain negative, so the label is tirzepatide-only, and whether the effect belongs to the class is disputed. Lilly's next-generation orals: one filed Jun 2036, under review. Survodutide MASH sNDA is still pending. Incretin market ≈$235B in 2036. US ≈$213B: ≈93.4M paying users (102.4M − 9.0M imports) × ≈$190 average net × 12. Ex-US ≈$22B and eroding.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of voluntary stops. Diarrhoea is more common on the bimagrumab combination. Restart nausea after drug holidays is a routine complaint.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Rising in absolute numbers with the larger and older user base.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Counterfeit-product reporting confounds the data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MDL litigation ongoing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈2.3M long-term older users meet sarcopenia criteria in Medicare claims. Lean mass is ~30–40% of loss in untrained users over 50 on monotherapy. The combination cuts this to ≈12% in trials, but Medicare users mostly cannot get it at the statutory rate.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label; body-composition monitoring in high-dose and combination labels; CMS annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users unchanged.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈10.5M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. 10.5M × ~0.6%/yr baseline hip-fracture rate × 0.35 excess ≈ 22,000 excess hip fractures a year, against ~315,000 US total. There are no fracture data for the combination. DEXA waits are 8–14 weeks.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelling retained; bone endpoints in all filings; CMS 90-day bone-pause code unchanged; DOJ civil case against Novo settled in 2035 without admission.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Relative risk ≈1.7 class-wide. 102.4M users × ~4/100,000 baseline × 0.7 excess ≈ 2,900 excess cases a year, mostly partial and permanent vision loss in one eye, higher with diabetes and rapid escalation. Ophthalmology referral volume from incretin users is up about a third on 2034.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The May 2034 class Warnings and Precautions statement is retained. The 2035 label update recommends a baseline eye exam for users with diabetes or aged 65+ and carries the warning into the pediatric and combination labels. Not boxed. The first MDL bellwether trial is set for 2037.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning removed Jan 2026; not returned.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The 2032 figures stand: ~12% of 12 mg retatrutide users versus ~5% of comparators. ≈11M people are now on top-dose regimens. In older MCI users, apathy from the drug cannot be told apart from apathy from the disease. An NIH-funded randomised low-dose trial began enrolling in 2036.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FTC consent orders stand; no label change.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Employer retreat produced the largest wave of coverage-driven stops yet, at ≈4M people over 2035–36. Most moved to cash or diabetes codes, and ≈1.5M stayed off.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CMS bone-pause code softens it for Medicare; no private-plan rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Common in high-loss older users, gray-market users and, newly, in MCI patients whose intake was already poor.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; Part D counselling screen.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of follow-up. The 2035 adolescent readout showed a small lag in bone-mineral accrual (≈−0.3 z-score at 2 years) of uncertain clinical meaning. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Adolescent labels updated with bone-accrual language; postmarketing requirements continue.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈9.0M imported or counterfeit users; growth slowed after the portal cut. Poison-centre calls are flat on 2034. Smaller contamination clusters continue in Georgia and Alabama, with no event on the 2033 scale.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA import alerts expanded; Safe Pens bill still stalled; no individual prosecutions.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded from emerging. Pressed 50 mg tablets are now the largest single counterfeit category by seizure count, with 0–300% of labelled content.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warnings; NABP verified-pharmacy guidance; no new law.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in long-term 65+ users. MCI users are a new high-risk subgroup.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening mandatory in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Worse in over-50s who were cut off by the 2035 employer coverage withdrawals.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Joint society guidance issued in 2035; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A several-bpm mean rise at 12 mg retatrutide; CV outcomes trial still ongoing.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Precautionary label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Muscle spasms in roughly a third of combination users early on, usually transient. Acne is more common in younger users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled at approval.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass preserved on DEXA without matching strength or function gain
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Early registry data in untrained combination users show DEXA lean mass held but grip strength and chair-rise times no better than on tirzepatide alone. Bone effects of activin-receptor blockade at scale are unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA postmarketing requirement for functional and fracture outcomes; label claims mass, not strength.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth and pubertal timing in children 6–11
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈110k users; trial follow-up was too short to assess final height or pubertal timing.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Growth and DEXA monitoring in the label; 10-year registry required.

food_and_beverage.state: With 37% of adults on the drug, salty-snack volume falls ~4–5% a year and confectionery ~6%. Two PE-held candy portfolios merged. Protein and fortified dairy lead. The backlash sustains a growing 'real food' and 'nature's GLP-1' supplement segment of berberine, fibre and fermented products, sold heavily through Christian bookstores and wellness influencers. Discount grocers still push calorie-dense value packs to people who are off. School cafeteria vendors now plan around medicated 6–11-year-olds.

alcohol.state: Ninth straight year of spirits volume decline; beer down; non-alcoholic formats grow. Tobacco and vape keep falling faster than the old trend.

restaurants.state: Spend per cover is down ~13% from 2028 in high-uptake suburbs, and gram-priced menus are standard. The backlash props up a counter-segment: Southern 'meat-and-three' and buffet formats in Nashville, Knoxville and Birmingham market 'no grams, no scales'. Holiday-weekend traffic spikes as drug holidays sync with Fridays.

apparel.state: The 'structured' and 'cycle' split holds. Combination users fuel a premium 'retained' category. A small fat-positive label revival, led by brands in Oakland and Brooklyn, wins press and some mid-market shelf space; plus sizing stops shrinking for the first time since 2027.

fitness.state: Medicare Advantage prescribed lifting continues to grow. Premium DEXA-coaching chains lose some members to the combination, whose ads imply lifting is optional. Combination-user registries suggest it is not, and the chains now market 'strength, not just mass'.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage is down to 46% of employers. Coverage concentrates on diabetes, cardiac, sleep-apnoea and CKD codes, and audits of 'code migration' (prediabetes coded up, borderline A1c retests) are a new PBM product. Pharmacy trend has slowed to ~+5% as net price falls. Life insurers still price untreated BMI ≥30. Bone, fall and eye costs land on Part A and MA.

pharma.state: Volume up ~30% over two years and net price down ~10%. Lilly leads on tirzepatide (with the MCI label), the combination and retatrutide. Novo holds the pill and pediatrics. Amgen's MariTide takes a niche. The parked generic has turned into an appeals-court case. Indian and Chinese makers dominate abroad.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Still income, now with a fourth reading. 'Retained' (lean with combination-held muscle) reads as top-third. The soft 'pill body' reads as middle. Visible regain around the middle reads as lost coverage. A deliberately unmedicated larger body increasingly reads as a statement, religious, political or fat-positive, rather than as an inability to afford the drug.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Bottom-third use (32.8%) still trails the top (41%). The middle third took the employer retreat. Families who were covered in 2034 now pay $199 a person on the portal, or pick which spouse stays on. Bodies keep diverging by regimen, and the combination widens the gap at the top while Medicare's oldest users wait on a coverage ruling.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first meals remain the default among users. In Nashville the backlash has made the full table a liturgy. Several megachurches run 'Unmeasured Sunday' potlucks with no scales and no grams, and the 'meat-and-three' revival there is the clearest local market signal. Family dinners now often include a medicated 9-year-old.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps added 'holiday weekends' to their filters. 'Unmedicated' has grown from a niche into a sizeable identity tag, clustered among evangelical singles and queer fat-positive communities, two groups that otherwise have little in common.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Contested again. A visible counter-movement brings together a fat-acceptance revival, anti-pharma 'natural' influencers, and evangelical pastors who preach appetite as God-given and the grey as spiritual numbness. The under-12 approval gave it its strongest argument and its largest rallies. It has no unified platform: one wing wants the drugs cheaper and optional, another wants them kept from children, another wants them gone.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Data are unchanged from 2032 (~12% vs ~5% at 12 mg retatrutide), but exposure is larger: ≈11M people on top-dose regimens imply about 770k excess clinically meaningful anhedonia cases if the association is causal. ≈5.8M 'calm' and 'focus' subscribers remain unmeasured until the NIH trial reads out. In a 2036 national survey ≈41% of users report a planned drug holiday or dose-down in the past six months, most often citing 'feeling flat' rather than GI effects.
interior_life.framing: A side effect everyone discusses and manages, like caffeine crashes. People say 'I'm a bit grey this week' at work. Drug holidays are scheduled in apps, and telehealth brands sell 'weekend dose' packs. Clinicians still say 'reward modulation'. For MCI patients' families the question is whether the apathy comes from the drug or the disease.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Managers routinely hear 'I'm on a holiday weekend, I'll be sharp Monday.' Hospitality and sales staff still dose down before peaks. Lifestyle-account 'focus' reimbursement continues where weight coverage was cut. Employees resent that the employer will pay for focus but not for weight. Tenure gates survive at the employers that still cover.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Holiday art' is a recognised genre: albums and stand-up sets made in deliberate off-weeks and marketed as such. Nashville songwriters bill 'written unmedicated' shows. Escape rooms and extreme sports keep growing, and spicy-food competitions are a fixture on drug-holiday weekends.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists build treatment plans around holiday weekends. Couples synchronise or deliberately stagger holidays. Adult children of MCI patients argue over whether a parent's flatness is the price of keeping their memory.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Body politics joined price politics. Presidential primary candidates in 2036 were asked about under-12 approval and about 'feeling grey'. The backlash is a visible voting bloc in Tennessee, Kentucky and Oklahoma. Mainstream candidates of both parties take credit for the portal price cut. No new state action resulted.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding and approving. It cleared the combination, the under-12 indication and the MCI indication, each with monitoring requirements, and extended the NAION class warning with eye-exam recommendations. It declared the first-filer exclusivity forfeited and is defending that in court. It brings no individual prosecutions, and Congress has passed no import or authentication law. The FTC consent orders stand.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Unchanged: permanent Part D obesity benefit at $199 with a $50 copay; 90% Medicaid match for the same 31 states plus DC. CMS has not decided whether the bimagrumab combination qualifies for the statutory rate. The Jul 2035 HHS portal agreement is a voluntary pricing commitment, not a statute.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard is unchanged: ≥80% PDC, verified six-monthly weights, 5% response or clinician override, annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users, 90-day bone-pause code, two misses suspend coverage for 6 months. Clinician overrides for MCI patients who do not lose 5% are rising. Private kiosk gating shrank as employers dropped coverage, but PBMs now mine A1c and claims data to audit code migration.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnoea screening still pushes drivers toward tirzepatide. Large fleets keep voluntary visual-field checks, and there is no FMCSA rule. Army accession policy is still contested; Air Force waivers continue.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The Jul 2035 portal deal traded price cuts for Section 232 tariff relief on manufacturers' US-filled product, so supply diplomacy now sets domestic prices. Chinese API and Indian finished product still feed the 9M-user gray market. The Telangana import alert remains an irritant with India.

events.event: In three weeks, two drugmakers file three applications. Lilly files tirzepatide/bimagrumab after phase 3 shows 22% loss with lean mass about 12% of loss. It also files a tirzepatide sNDA after a 3-year trial in adults with mild cognitive impairment and obesity or diabetes cut progression to dementia by 21%. Novo files semaglutide for children aged 6–11

Annual benefits surveys show employers covering weight-management incretins fell from 64% to 52% in a year. Three of the ten largest US retailers and a major benefits administrator's default plan cut obesity coverage while keeping diabetes, cardiac and sleep-apnoea codes. By late 2036 coverage is 46%

Novo and Lilly sign new three-year HHS portal commitments: injectable maintenance at $199–249, the 50 mg pill at $199 and retatrutide at $349, in exchange for Section 232 tariff relief. The next month FDA declares the first generic filer's exclusivity forfeited, and the D.C. Circuit stays the decision, so no generic launches

FDA approves Lilly's tirzepatide/bimagrumab combination, labelled for lean-mass preservation but not strength or fracture, and semaglutide for obese children aged 6–11 with DEXA and growth monitoring. Both labels carry the NAION class warning with new baseline eye-exam advice. Lilly's launch line is 'Lose the weight. Keep yourself.'
events.driver: next_gen_launch: muscle_preserving_combo; new_indications: pediatric_under_12; safety_signal: vision_class_label

events.event: FDA approves tirzepatide to reduce progression from mild cognitive impairment to dementia in adults with obesity or type 2 diabetes. Under existing Part D eligibility, about 1.6M Medicare beneficiaries carry an MCI code on the drug by year end, and memory clinics report waitlists

Tens of thousands rally in Nashville for 'Unmeasured Sunday', drawing evangelical congregations, fat-acceptance groups and 'natural health' influencers in protest at the under-12 approval. The same month a national survey finds 41% of users took a planned drug holiday in the past six months, most citing 'feeling grey'

open_tensions: CMS has not ruled whether the muscle-preserving combination qualifies for the $199 statutory rate. So the oldest, frailest users with the most bone and fall risk, who are also the new MCI population, are the ones least able to get the drug marketed as solving frailty. Its functional and fracture benefits are unproven.

Employer retreat pushed coverage onto diabetes and cardiac codes. PBMs now audit 'code migration' while the middle third pays $199 a person on a voluntary portal deal that expires in 2038 and is tied to tariff diplomacy.

The generic forfeiture sits before the D.C. Circuit. A ruling for FDA could put generic semaglutide on shelves within months and break the managed-decline pricing. A ruling against it parks the generic until the first filer's plant clears inspection.

About 110k children aged 6–11, mostly on Medicaid under EPSDT, are on a weekly injectable with no final-height, puberty or adult-bone data. The backlash's largest constituency formed around them, and the drug's flattening effect remains unmeasured in both children and dementia-risk elders.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is on the US market; generic_us remains false.
The permanent Part D obesity benefit still pays the $199/month negotiated rate with a $50 beneficiary copay, eligibility BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity, and the counselling visit.
The CMS continuation standard is unchanged, including the 90-day 'bone pause' code, and the same 31 states plus DC use it for the 90% Medicaid match; no state joined or left.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer direct channels.
The FTC consent orders still bar 'anxiety treatment' claims while permitting 'calm' and 'focus' marketing for low-dose subscription products.

prose.headline: Cheaper Pill, No Coverage: Your Job Dropped the Drug, Your Mother Needs It for Memory, and Nashville Wants It Gone
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 more than a third of American adults, about a hundred million people, are on an incretin drug. The price fell and coverage fell with it. In the summer of 2035 Novo and Lilly agreed new portal prices with HHS in exchange for tariff relief. Maintenance pens now cost $199 to $249 a month and the fifty-milligram pill $199. Employers had already started leaving. Twelve months earlier nearly two-thirds of them covered the drug for weight. Now fewer than half do. Most kept paying for diabetes, heart disease and sleep apnoea, so the drug follows the diagnosis. Doctors retest borderline blood sugars and PBMs sell audits of what they call code migration. Families that were covered in 2034 now pay cash and sometimes decide which spouse stays on.

Generic semaglutide still has not arrived. The FDA declared the first filer's exclusivity forfeited, the company appealed, and a federal court froze the decision. About nine million people still buy imported or counterfeit product, mostly the pressed pills now. That number has grown more slowly since the portal price came down.

Three approvals changed who takes the drug. In December 2035 Lilly launched a combination that pairs tirzepatide with bimagrumab, an antibody that keeps muscle from wasting. On scans the weight comes off with most of the muscle intact. The ads say the frailty problem is solved. The label says only that lean mass is preserved, and early registry data show people keeping the muscle mass without getting any stronger. The combination costs $549 a month direct. Medicare has not decided whether its fixed $199 rate applies, so the people most at risk of falls cannot get it unless they pay cash.

The same month, semaglutide was approved for obese children aged six to eleven, with bone scans and growth charts written into the label. About a hundred thousand children now take it, most of them on Medicaid, which by law must cover what is medically necessary for children. In March tirzepatide became the first incretin approved to slow progression from mild cognitive impairment to dementia, in people who also have obesity or diabetes. The effect is modest, about a fifth fewer conversions over three years. Within months a million and a half Medicare beneficiaries had an MCI code and a prescription. In memory clinics, adult children now ask whether their parent's new flatness comes from the disease or from the drug that is meant to slow it. Nobody can tell them.

Every box carries the optic-nerve warning, and the new labels add an eye exam. At this scale the warning implies nearly three thousand excess cases a year of one-eyed vision loss. Ophthalmologists have a new referral stream. About twenty-two thousand excess hip fractures a year are billed to the part of Medicare that does not pay for the drug.

The flatness people call the grey is now an ordinary complaint, mentioned the way people mention a bad night's sleep. Four in ten users took a planned drug holiday in the last six months. Apps schedule them, telehealth brands sell weekend doses, and couples coordinate them. Nashville songwriters advertise shows written off the drug.

The pediatric approval gave a scattered resistance a rallying point. In May tens of thousands gathered in Nashville under the banner Unmeasured Sunday: megachurch congregations, fat-acceptance activists, natural-health influencers. They agree that appetite is not a disease and on very little else. One wing wants the drug cheaper and optional, another wants it kept away from children, and a third wants it gone. Meat-and-three restaurants across Tennessee have hung no-scales signs. Plus-size racks have stopped shrinking.

No new law passed and no state changed course. From the outside it looks like a health system working, with lower prices, new indications and better results. What has changed is who pays and which bodies come out of it intact.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Lorraine Petty is fifty-three and takes the fasting blood draw at 6:40, before her shift scheduling trucks at a distribution centre outside Dayton. Her A1c last spring was 6.3. At 6.5 the plan's diabetes code would cover her pen again. She almost wants it high.

Since March she has been on the $199 pill, paid through the portal on a card she keeps for nothing else. It costs about what her car insurance does. Her husband stopped in January so she could keep going. His belt has gone back two notches. Neither of them says anything about it.

At lunch her coworker Darnell says he's on a holiday weekend and plans to eat a whole brisket. They laugh. Lorraine skipped hers last month and cried at a dog food commercial, and she liked it.

After work she drives to her mother's in Kettering. June is seventy-six and has had a memory code since April, and Part D charges her fifty dollars. The pharmacy sheet says eye exam in bold. June's appointment is in September. June asks twice whether Lorraine's daughter is still in Columbus. She is quieter than she used to be, and Lorraine can't tell whether she is better or worse.

On the way home she passes a church sign: UNMEASURED SUNDAY, ALL WELCOME, BRING A DISH. Her granddaughter, who is nine, starts her shots next month. The Medicaid letter came Tuesday.

The lab portal pings at 9:12. A1c 6.4. She sits in the driveway and doesn't go in yet.

rationale.badness: The world keeps every 2034 harm and adds more. That is a harder society with new losers, though not collapse, so it sits above 2026 but below the 7 anchor.
